rod.label: Warrior with a Rod of Teleport Other next to a hill giant
rod.explanation: Grid danger 64 against 106 hit points. Original: borg_caution() chooses nothing (the defence never considers the rod), and the attack step queues melee on the giant (keys +6); the rod is not used. Corrected: borg_caution() chooses the Teleport Other defence and queues *p65zb5 (target the giant, zap the rod in slot b, use the target). The real zap command fails three times (the game's device failure chance for this Warrior is 24.2%) and succeeds on the fourth attempt: the giant is moved from (11,12) to (38,22), 33 grids away, and the rod starts recharging.

wand.label: Control: the same Warrior with a Wand of Teleport Other
wand.explanation: The same scene with the wand instead of the rod. Both versions choose the defence, aim the wand (keys *p65ab5), and the real aim command teleports the giant to (38,22) at the first attempt (10 charges left). This case runs through both changed lines (the wand is accepted before the rod check and aimed before the zap). The logs are byte-identical.

weak.label: Control: rod carried, harmless soldier ant adjacent
weak.explanation: The same Warrior with the rod, next to a soldier ant (grid danger 2 against 106 hit points). No danger to speak of, so borg_caution() chooses nothing and neither version zaps the rod; both queue melee (keys +6). The logs are byte-identical. This control shows the rod is not zapped at harmless monsters; it does not reach the changed lines.
